name: Isaac Israëls
bio: Isaac Lazarus Israëls was a Dutch painter associated with the Amsterdam Impressionism movement.

paintings.title: Riding Donkeys on the Beach
paintings.story: Riding Donkeys on the Beach or The Donkey Ride is an oil on canvas painting executed by the Dutch artist Isaac Israëls, created c. 1898-1900. It is held in the Rijksmuseum, in Amsterdam.
facts: Israëls lived in Amsterdam since 1886, but from the mid-1890s he often returned to The Hague, where his father Jozef Israëls lived, for the Summer.
He usually rented a villa at the Oranjehotel in Scheveningen, where he would stay.

paintings.title: Two Girls in the Snow
paintings.story: Two Girls in the Snow is an oil on panel painting by the Dutch artist Isaac Israëls, from c. 1890–1894. It depicts two girls, facing heavy cold, in a city street. It is held in the Rijksmuseum, in Amsterdam.
facts: This is one of Israel's few preserved paintings from the early 1890s, with which he was apparently satisfied.
It depicts two factory or studio girls, at full-length, caught by the painter as they are passing on the street.

paintings.title: Portrait of a Wounded KNIL Soldier
paintings.story: Portrait of a Wounded KNIL Soldier is an Amsterdam impressionist portrait painting by Isaac Israëls, signed and dated to 1882. It has been in the Rijksmuseum since 2000.
facts: The artist Pieter Hugo made a portrait photograph that nods both to this impressionist painting and to the realistic painting of Jan Kooi.

paintings.title: Woman in Profile in Front of Van Gogh's Sunflowers
paintings.story: Woman in Profile in Front of Van Gogh's Sunflowers is an oil on canvas painting by the Dutch painter Isaac Israëls, from 1918. It depicts a bare-chested female model in front of a version of Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers. It is held at the Museum de Fundatie, in Zwolle.
facts: In 1917, after much hesitation, Isaac Israëls moved into his father Jozef's former studio in The Hague.
He had just been loaned two paintings by Van Gogh from Johanna van Gogh-Bonger, the widow of Vincent's brother Theo van Gogh.

paintings.title: Shop Window (Israëls)
paintings.story: Shop Window is an oil on canvas painting by the Dutch artist Isaac Israëls, from c. 1894-1898. It depicts a street scene with passers-by viewing the window of a fashion store. The work is held in the Rijksmuseum, in Amsterdam. It is part of the legacy of the art collectors couple Drucker-Fraser.
facts: Around 1900, for example, he depicted various activities at the Hirsch & Cie fashion house on Leidseplein, commissioned by the owner.
Like fellow Impressionist George Hendrik Breitner, Israëls was fascinated by urban street life since he arrived in Amsterdam in 1886.

paintings.title: Ippy and Gertie Posing at Fashion House Hirsch, Amsterdam
paintings.story: Ippy and Gertie Posing at Fashion House Hirsch, Amsterdam is a circa 1916 oil on canvas painting by the Dutch artist Isaac Israëls. It depicts the twin sisters Helena (1895–1964) and Geertruida Wehmann (1895–1975), models at the Amsterdam fashion house Hirsch & Cie in the Leidseplein whose professional names were Ippy and Gertie respectively.
facts: Although Breitner sketched with van Gogh in their student days at The Hague (Breitner was later dismissive of Vincent's "eskimo paintings", while Vincent in turn dismissed Breitner's efforts as "mouldy wallpaper"), there is no record of Israëls ever meeting van Gogh.
There their modelling talent was discovered and they went to work at the very fashionable Maison Lucile at 24 Burlington Street, whose clients included aristocracy, royalty, and theatre celebrities.
